summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR3,337 crore and EBITDA rose 27% QoQ to INR138 crore, but margin stayed thin at 4.2%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was about INR3,337 crore, up 58% YoY and 22% QoQ, with H1 revenue of about INR6,061 crore. EBITDA was about INR138 crore (4.2% margin) versus INR109 crore (4.0%) in Q1, and PAT rose about 30% QoQ to INR90 crore. Copper volumes drove growth, with the new copper anode plant contributing its first sales, while working capital days fell to 49 from 66 at FY26-end and net debt/equity improved to about 0.5x from 0.7x. Management said margins may moderate as copper mix shifts, and most expansion items (cathode, wire rod, busbar, antimony, plastic) are slated for Q3 or Q4 FY27, with Kuwait delayed by West Asia logistics.

+55% YoY per CEO opening remarks; CFO stated about 65%
+27% QoQ from INR109 crore in Q1 FY27
vs INR250 crore in H1 FY26, roughly flat

segments.name: Copper and copper ingots
segments.commentary: Q2 sales volume about 16,411 MT, up about 73% YoY from 9,434 MT and up from 14,683 MT in Q1. Segment EBITDA rose to INR61 crore from INR46 crore, with EBITDA per ton up to INR37,237 from INR31,825. Copper including the new initiative was 8% of revenue, while management also said copper is over 65% of turnover.

segments.name: Lead and lead alloy ingots
segments.commentary: Q2 volume about 34,851 MT, up from about 32,150 MT in Q1 but below year-ago levels. EBITDA rose to INR67 crore from INR60 crore, and EBITDA per ton to INR19,310 from INR18,660. Management said lead is about 30% of turnover.

segments.name: Aluminium and aluminium alloys
segments.commentary: Q2 volume about 2,493 MT, up from 2,201 MT in Q1. Segment EBITDA rose to INR5.3 crore from INR4.7 crore.

segments.name: Value-added copper (Jain Green Technologies, anode plant)
segments.commentary: Both 800 MT/month anode phases commissioned (1,600 MT/month total), Phase II in trial run. H1 FY27 value-added sales about 3,575 MT. Management cited about INR14,434 per ton of separate EBITDA for this business, which is expected to rise with utilisation.

segments.name: Jain CY Circular Solutions (Ahmedabad subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Commenced commercial operations and booked about INR25.4 crore of revenue in Q2. Input capacity is about 71,000 MT/year of scrap, with output of about 25,000 MT/year of copper products at full ramp.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of more than 30% (30-40% range cited) for FY27, subject to market conditions and execution; management cited a 10-year average of about 40% CAGR.
Copper EBITDA per ton expected to keep rising with value-added products, per Kamlesh Jain, though management also flagged likely EBITDA margin moderation as copper mix scales.
Cathode Phase I (750 MT/month) commissioning imminent; Phase II targeted Q4 FY27. Wire rod (600 MT/month) and busbar and profiles (1,500 MT/month) targeted Q3 FY27.
Working capital cycle expected to range 50-70 days going forward, with quarterly swings of 10-20 days.
Management said FY27 volumes should rise, but declined to give segment-wise volume guidance on the call and will share it by email.
Management expects a copper cathode sale this quarter, and about 750 MT of cathode and about 600 MT of wire rod production in FY27.
capex_capacity: Copper anode plant: Phase I and II each 800 MT/month, total 1,600 MT/month installed; Phase II in trial run.

Copper cathode plant: 1,500 MT/month total in two 750 MT/month phases. Phase I civil work complete and commissioning at an advanced stage; Phase II targeted Q4 FY27. Phase I capex about INR120 crore (value-added copper total, about 60% of total capex attributed to cathode), Phase II expected to be lower.
Copper wire rod (600 MT/month) and busbar and profiles (1,500 MT/month) targeted for Q3 FY27.

Antimony recovery facility about 100 MT/month targeted Q3 FY27; dedicated plastic recycling plant capex about INR15 crore, operations targeted Q3 FY27 (management said early production has started at the shed).

Kuwait facility: machinery fully manufactured but shipment delayed by West Asia war and lack of specialised containers; management expects shipment within about 30 days and gave no firm execution timeline. It is intended as a lead ingot sourcing point.
demand_pricing: Sourcing shifted toward domestic: management said domestic share of total purchases is about 38-39% across metals, and local sourcing now exceeds 50-60% per Kamlesh Jain. Domestic scrap prices track LME and landed cost, so there is no direct cost benefit; the benefit is lower working capital.

Lead sourcing is challenged by shipping disruption and high freight from the Middle East. Management is offsetting with local purchases and new sourcing areas, and expects to manage Q3 without problems.
Management said raw material for the next four months is secured and expects no sourcing problem this fiscal year. Lead volumes rose about 8% QoQ.
Management said RCM on e-waste scrap will help only marginally unless GST on scrap purchases is reduced.

Competition: management positioned JRRL as a diversified multi-metal player (copper over 65% of turnover) versus lead-focused peers Gravita and POCL, and said the three cannot be compared like-for-like.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex for the copper cathode plant and is Phase II similar?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR120 crore covers the entire value-added copper capex (land, building, power, machines), with cathode about 60% of it. Phase II is lower, roughly 25-30% less per Mayank Pareek.

qa_highlights.question: Why has working capital fallen and has sourcing changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Jain attributed the decline to internal cash accumulation and a shift to local sourcing (now over 50-60%), which avoids pre-paid overseas purchases that tie up about two months of cash in transit.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic sourcing share has been flat at about 38-39%, and when will lead volumes return to 45,000-50,000 MT per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Hemant Jain said domestic sourcing is about 38-39% of total purchases across all metals. Kamlesh Jain said lead volumes rose about 8% QoQ but fell YoY, and gave no date for returning to the 45,000-50,000 MT run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Will copper EBITDA per ton keep rising, and what is the value-add per stage?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Jain said copper EBITDA per ton rose from INR30,000 to about INR37,500 and should keep rising. Mayank Pareek said cathode adds 1-1.5% to the bottom line, wire rod another 1-1.5%, and the average uplift across the chain is 2-3%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Jain said revenue growth of more than 30% (around 30-40%) is expected for FY27, subject to market conditions, and gave no margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why do the MTM figures differ between other income and operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Hemant Jain said other income includes MTM on open options, while the figure in COGS includes expired options and open futures tied to inventory or sales hedges. He offered to send a detailed reconciliation by email.

risks_watch: Kuwait plant delayed by West Asia logistics; no firm timeline given.
Lead volumes still below year-ago levels; sourcing depends on freight and shipping routes.
Copper EBITDA margin likely to moderate as value-added mix rises; value-added EBITDA per ton still in ramp-up.
Working capital cycle expected to swing 50-70 days.
Several projects (cathode Phase I, wire rod, busbar, antimony, plastic) depend on Q3 and Q4 FY27 commissioning; ramp-up and LME-grade cathode quality are unproven.
Management withheld segment-wise volume guidance and detailed MTM reconciliation, deferring them to email follow-up.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and sourcing, with the chairman repeatedly stating high confidence in FY27 raw material and revenue growth. More cautious and evasive on specifics: no segment volume guidance, no Kuwait timeline, and no margin commitment, and quarter-on-quarter comparisons were deflected as a commodity business.
key_quotes: I'm very confident up to this current year, March, we have all the raw material for next four months to come.
Copper alone contributes more than 65% of our turnover.
I would not like to give you an artificial or quarter-by-quarter margin commitment because as I said, it only yearly performance can be tracked
We are going to start. This year, this is the target.

growth.why: Management reiterates FY27 revenue growth above 30% (30-40% cited), backed by specific capacity coming live (cathode Phase I in trial, wire rod and busbar targeted Q3, cathode Phase II Q4), but Kuwait is delayed with no firm date and segment volume guidance was withheld, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was 4.2% in Q2 (up 14 bps QoQ from 4.0%) but management flagged likely moderation as copper mix scales, while copper EBITDA per ton rose to INR37,237 from INR31,825 and value-added EBITDA is about INR14,434 per ton and rising.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Cathode Phase I (750 MT/month) is commissioning now, wire rod (600 MT/month) and busbar (1,500 MT/month) are targeted Q3 FY27, cathode Phase II Q4 FY27 and antimony (100 MT/month) Q3 FY27, but Kuwait has no firm timeline due to West Asia logistics.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth above 30% (30-40% cited) and copper volume rose about 73% YoY to 16,411 MT in Q2, though lead volume of 34,851 MT remains below year-ago and no segment volume guidance was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed and management said it is building 'in a disciplined manner rather than rushing to ramp-up', so a fresh capex announcement is conditional on ramp-up of the current 2.5-3 quarters of projects; Kuwait is deferred.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue guidance was held at more than 30% (30-40% cited), and H1 revenue growth of about 55-65% gives room, but management gave no margin guidance and flagged moderation, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Kuwait is delayed with no firm timeline, lead volumes are still below year-ago levels (34,851 MT vs 45,000-50,000 MT run rate), and working capital is expected to swing 50-70 days, so project timing and volume could slip.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Copper cathode (Phase I now, Phase II Q4), wire rod, busbar and profiles, antimony recovery (about 100 MT/month) and plastic recycling (about INR15 crore capex, early production started) are all slated for Q3-Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Working capital cycle 50-70 days
rows.why: Cycle fell to 49 days from 66 at FY26-end on local sourcing (now 50-60%), but management guides a 50-70 day range with quarterly swings of 10-20 days.

rows.label: Net debt/equity down to about 0.5x
rows.why: Net debt to equity improved to about 0.5x from 0.7x at March 2026, with H1 operating cash flow of about INR129-130 crore.

rows.label: RCM on e-waste scrap limited benefit
rows.why: Management said RCM will help only marginally unless GST on scrap purchases is reduced, so no material tailwind is expected.
